analysis:
Reviewed the head text of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (lines 1-889). Changes visible: (1) planModels now sends a ClusterControlRequest carrying context.settings.servingScope (line 600); (2) the leader's executeForwarded passes request.scope into localPlanModels/localAdopt (lines 272, 276); (3) new planningScope(_:) (lines 609-611) picks forwarded scope, then local setting, then saved leadership scope, then defaults to .publicServing; (4) localPlanModels uses coordinator: !planningScope(scope).isLocalOnly (line 633) and shows the 'public traffic prohibited' text for private image qualification (line 672).

Security observations: the forwarded scope arrives over the paired, authenticated cluster link, and the peer was pinned via Secure Enclave pairing, so the scope is only a hint from a paired peer. The default is the stricter, coordinator-bound public serving, which fails safe. The routed() path refuses forwarding under privateImageQualification (lines 214-216), so the scope field cannot override that qualification. This does not touch the TB-002 plaintext legs, the App Attest authorization (TB-011), prefix-cache storage (T-041) or attestation.

Not visible and left for later passes: the remainder of the file (localAdopt with scope, setScope and register at about lines 1048-1084), the ClusterControlRequest scope encoding and validation, and how the adopted scope is persisted and used at serve time. I cannot confirm that a paired peer's scope cannot widen serving beyond what the owner approved on this Mac. That depends on localAdopt/localSetScope and on ClusterServingScope validation, which are outside the supplied units. No concrete regression is identified in the supplied text.
